easy.def: Liking one thing more in an unfair way.
examples: The judge showed no bias.
Bias is unfair.
A bias for one team.

more.def: An unfair liking or dislike for one person or thing over another, without good reason.
examples: The referee showed no bias and treated both teams fairly.
A bias for one team can make you an unfair judge.
The news story was written with a bias.

easy.def: Not fair to everyone.
examples: The referee was biased.
I saw a biased story.
The judge was not biased.

more.def: Favoring one side unfairly.
examples: The referee was biased and favored one team.
A biased story only told one side.
The judges said they would not be biased.

easy.def: A cloth tied under a baby's chin to keep food off clothes.
examples: The baby wears a bib.
The bib is wet.
Put on your bib.

more.def: A cloth or piece of plastic tied under a chin to keep clothes clean while eating.
examples: The baby wore a bib to catch the spills.
A bib kept his shirt clean.
She wiped the bib after lunch.

easy.def: A holy book that many people read in church.
examples: The family has a Bible.
She reads the Bible.
There are stories in the Bible.

more.def: The holy book of the Christian religion, and the first part is also holy to Jews.
examples: The family read from the Bible.
Many stories in the Bible are very old.
The Bible has been translated into many languages.

easy.def: Having to do with the Bible.
examples: It is a biblical story.
The biblical tale of Noah.
A biblical name.

more.def: Having to do with the Bible, or found in it.
examples: The story of Noah and the ark is a biblical tale.
David is a biblical name.
The painting showed a biblical scene.

easy.def: The big muscle at the front of your upper arm.
examples: He flexed his biceps.
The biceps is a muscle.
Her biceps are strong.

more.def: A large muscle on the front of the upper arm that bends the elbow.
examples: He flexed his biceps to show how strong he was.
Lifting weights makes the biceps bigger.
The biceps helps you bend your arm.

easy.def: To argue about small things.
examples: The kids bicker.
They bickered over the toy.
Do not bicker.

more.def: To argue in a petty way about small things.
examples: The sisters bickered over who sat by the window.
They bickered about whose turn it was.
Do not bicker about little things.

easy.def: A two-wheeled vehicle you ride by pedaling.
examples: I ride my bicycle.
The bicycle has a bell.
She got a new bicycle.

more.def: A vehicle with two wheels that you ride by pushing pedals with your feet.
examples: I ride my bicycle to school.
The bicycle has a bell and a basket.
She got a new bicycle for her birthday.

easy.def: An offer of a price.
examples: He made a bid for the painting.
My bid was ten dollars.
The highest bid wins.

more.def: An offer to pay a certain amount of money for something.
examples: He made a bid of ten dollars for the painting.
The highest bid won the old clock.
Her bid was too low.

easy.def: To offer a price for something.
examples: I bid ten dollars.
She bid on the lamp.
He bid for the toy.

more.def: To offer an amount of money for something, as at an auction.
examples: I bid ten dollars for the chair.
She bid on the old lamp.
They bid against each other for the painting.

easy.def: A person who offers money for something at a sale.
examples: The bidder raised her hand.
The highest bidder won.
A bidder at the sale.

more.def: A person who offers an amount of money for something at an auction.
examples: The highest bidder won the painting at the auction.
A bidder raised his hand to offer fifty dollars.
Bidders gathered at the school fair to bid on baskets.

easy.def: Offering how much money you will pay at a sale.
examples: The bidding started at five dollars.
The bidding was fast.
Bidding went up quickly.

more.def: The act of offering a price for something at an auction.
examples: The bidding for the painting began at ten dollars.
Bidding at the school auction was quick and exciting.
The bidding stopped when no one offered a higher price.

easy.def: What someone tells you to do.
examples: The dog did my bidding.
He did his mom's bidding.
The servant did the king's bidding.

more.def: A command or request that you are expected to follow.
examples: In the story, the genie does whatever his master asks and does his bidding.
The knights did the king's bidding.
She did her teacher's bidding and handed out the papers.

easy.def: To wait for the right time.
examples: I bide my time.
She bided her time.
He will bide.

more.def: To wait patiently for a good moment to do something.
examples: The cat bided its time before it pounced.
She bided her time until the line got shorter.
He bided his time and waited for his turn.

easy.def: Large in size.
examples: An elephant is big.
I have a big dog.
It is a big house.

more.def: Large in size, amount, or importance.
examples: A big wave crashed onto the sandy beach.
The school is having a big party for the end of the year.
Winning the contest was a big moment for her.

easy.def: A two-wheeled machine you pedal.
examples: I ride my bike.
My bike is red.
She rode her bike to school.

more.def: A vehicle with two wheels that you move by pushing pedals.
examples: I ride my bike to school.
She pumped air into her bike tires.
We went for a long bike ride.

easy.def: A person who rides a bike.
examples: The biker rode up the hill.
A biker passed us.
The biker wore a helmet.

more.def: A person who rides a bicycle or a motorcycle.
examples: The biker wore a helmet and rode carefully down the path.
A group of bikers rode through the park on Saturday.
The biker stopped at the red light.

easy.def: A swimsuit that comes in two small pieces.
examples: She wore a bikini at the beach.
The bikini is yellow.
A bikini dries fast.

more.def: A two-piece swimsuit worn at the beach or pool.
examples: She packed a bikini and a towel for the beach trip.
The pool store sold a red bikini and a blue one.
A bikini was drying on the line next to the towels.

easy.def: The hard part of a bird's mouth.
examples: The duck has a flat bill.
The bird dipped its bill in the water.
A pelican has a big bill.

more.def: The hard, pointed or flat part of a bird's mouth; a beak.
examples: The woodpecker tapped on the tree with its strong bill.
A hummingbird has a long, thin bill for sipping nectar.
The duck dipped its wide bill into the pond.

easy.def: A paper that tells how much money you must pay.
examples: Dad paid the bill.
The bill came after lunch.
Mom read the bill.

more.def: A written list that shows how much money you owe for things you bought or used.
examples: The waiter brought the bill after we finished dinner.
The electric bill comes at the end of each month.
Dad checked the bill to make sure it was right.

easy.def: A very large sign beside a road.
examples: We saw a billboard.
The billboard was huge.
A billboard for pizza.

more.def: A very large sign beside a road or on a building that is used to advertise something.
examples: A giant billboard for ice cream stood beside the highway.
We read the billboard as we drove by.
The billboard showed a smiling family.

easy.def: A game played on a table with a stick and balls.
examples: They play billiards.
Billiards uses balls.
Billiards is a game.

more.def: A game played on a table with balls that you hit with a long stick.
examples: Dad plays billiards with his friends.
A billiards table has a green top.
Billiards is played with a long stick called a cue.

easy.def: A very big number, one thousand millions.
examples: There are billions of stars.
A billion is huge.
The country has a billion people.

more.def: The number 1,000,000,000, which is one thousand millions.
examples: There are billions of stars in the galaxy.
A billion is a thousand millions.
The earth has about eight billion people.

easy.def: A person with a thousand million dollars or more.
examples: The billionaire gave money.
A billionaire is very rich.
The billionaire built a school.

more.def: A person who has a billion dollars or more, so that they are very, very rich.
examples: The billionaire gave a large amount of money to build a new library.
A billionaire is someone with at least a thousand million dollars.
The billionaire owned a company that made computers.

easy.def: To swell out and roll like a big wave.
examples: The sail billowed.
Smoke billowed up.
The curtains billowed.

more.def: To swell out and roll in the wind like a big wave.
examples: The sails billowed in the strong wind.
Clouds of steam billowed from the pot.
Her skirt billowed as she ran.

easy.def: A big rolling wave of smoke or water.
examples: A billow of smoke rose.
Billows of fog rolled in.
The billows rocked the boat.

more.def: A large, rolling wave of something such as water, smoke or cloud.
examples: A billow of white steam rose from the train.
The ship rode over the billows of the sea.
Billows of fog rolled over the hill.

easy.def: A large container for storing things.
examples: Put the trash in the bin.
The toy bin is full.
The bin is blue.

more.def: A large box or container that is used for storing or collecting things.
examples: Put the recycling in the blue bin.
The toy bin in my room is full.
The grain was stored in a bin.

easy.def: To tie something together.
examples: I bind the sticks together.
She bound her hair.
We bound the books.

more.def: To tie or fasten things together tightly.
examples: I bound the sticks together with a string.
She bound her hair with a ribbon.
Dad bound the books with a rubber band.

easy.def: A cover with rings that holds papers.
examples: I put the paper in my binder.
My binder is blue.
Open your binder.

more.def: A cover with rings or clips that holds papers together.
examples: I put the worksheet in my binder.
My blue binder is full of notes.
The teacher asked us to open our binders.

easy.def: The cover that holds the pages of a book together.
examples: The book has a red binding.
The binding is strong.
The binding broke.

more.def: The cover and stitching that hold the pages of a book together, or something that holds something else together.
examples: The old book had a leather binding.
A strong binding keeps the pages from falling out.
The ski boot clicked into the binding.

easy.def: A tool you look through to see far away things up close.
examples: I looked through binoculars.
The binoculars are heavy.
We used binoculars to watch birds.

more.def: A tool with two small telescopes joined together, which you hold to your eyes to see things far away.
examples: I used binoculars to watch the birds in the tree.
The sailor looked through the binoculars at the distant ship.
The binoculars made the faraway mountain look close.

easy.def: A person who writes about someone's life.
examples: The biographer wrote a book.
A biographer tells a life story.
The biographer wrote about the president.

more.def: A writer who writes the story of another person's life.
examples: The biographer wrote a book about the famous scientist.
A biographer spent years studying her subject.
The biographer interviewed the family.

easy.def: A book about a person's life.
examples: I read a biography.
The biography is about a scientist.
A biography of a queen.

more.def: A book or a story that tells about the life of a real person, written by someone else.
examples: I read a biography of a famous scientist for my school report.
The biography told about her childhood and her career.
The library has biographies of presidents and explorers.

easy.def: Having to do with living things.
examples: Eating is a biological need.
Plants are biological things.
Growing is a biological process.

more.def: Having to do with living things and the study of life.
examples: The biological parts of a cell work together.
Breathing is a biological function of every animal.
The scientists studied the biological processes of plants.

easy.def: A scientist who studies plants and animals.
examples: A biologist studies plants.
The biologist looked at a frog.
My aunt is a biologist.

more.def: A scientist who studies living things such as plants, animals and tiny cells.
examples: The biologist counted the fish in the pond.
A biologist looked at pond water under a microscope.
The biologist studied how bees find flowers.

easy.def: The study of living things.
examples: I like biology.
Biology is science.
We study biology.

more.def: The science that studies plants, animals and all living things.
examples: I like biology class.
Biology teaches how animals live.
We studied plants in biology.

easy.def: An old airplane with two sets of wings.
examples: The biplane flew.
A biplane has four wings.
We saw a biplane.

more.def: An early kind of airplane with two sets of wings, one above the other.
examples: The old biplane flew over the field.
A biplane has two wings on each side.
The pilot waved from the cockpit of the biplane.

easy.def: A tree with thin white bark.
examples: The birch has white bark.
A birch grew by the lake.
We sat by a birch.

more.def: A slim tree with white or silvery bark that peels off in thin layers.
examples: The white bark of the birch glowed in the moonlight.
Birch trees grow in cool northern forests.
Canoes were once made from the bark of the birch.

easy.def: An animal with feathers and wings.
examples: A bird sings.
The bird built a nest.
Birds eat seeds.

more.def: An animal with feathers, wings and a beak, that usually can fly.
examples: A bird built a nest in the tree.
Penguins are birds that cannot fly.
Owls are birds that hunt at night.

easy.def: A cage for pet birds.
examples: The bird is in the birdcage.
A birdcage has bars.
The birdcage is big.

more.def: A cage with bars where a pet bird is kept.
examples: The parrot sat in its birdcage.
A birdcage hung by the window.
She cleaned the birdcage every week.

easy.def: A little bird.
examples: Look at the birdie.
The birdie sang.
A birdie sat on the fence.

more.def: A child's word for a small bird.
examples: Look at the pretty birdie!
The birdie sang in the tree.
A little birdie sat on the fence.

easy.def: The sweet sound that birds make.
examples: I love birdsong in the morning.
We heard birdsong.
Birdsong filled the woods.

more.def: The musical sounds that birds make, especially in the early morning.
examples: We woke up to the sound of birdsong outside the window.
Birdsong filled the woods in the early spring.
She recorded the birdsong with her tablet.

easy.def: When a baby comes into the world.
examples: We saw a picture from his birth.
The birth of a lamb is exciting.
Her birth was in the spring.

more.def: The time when a baby or animal is born.
examples: The farm was busy on the night of the foal's birth.
The nurse wrote the baby's weight at birth.
A birth certificate shows the date and place you were born.

easy.def: The day you were born, every year.
examples: Today is my birthday.
We have cake on my birthday.
Her birthday is in May.

more.def: The day each year that is the same date as the day you were born.
examples: My birthday is in the spring.
We sang to Grandpa on his birthday.
She turned eight on her birthday.

easy.def: Giving birth.
examples: The birthing of a calf.
Birthing takes time.
Birthing is hard.

more.def: The act of giving birth to a baby or young animal.
examples: The farmer watched the birthing of a calf.
The nurse helped with the birthing.
The zoo planned the birthing of the baby panda.

easy.def: A mark on the skin that you were born with.
examples: She has a birthmark.
A birthmark on his arm.
The birthmark is small.

more.def: A colored mark on the skin that a person has had since they were born.
examples: She has a small birthmark on her arm shaped like a heart.
A birthmark is something that you are born with.
He has a birthmark on his cheek.

easy.def: The place where someone was born.
examples: His birthplace is Texas.
The birthplace is small.
I visited my birthplace.

more.def: The town or place where a person was born.
examples: His birthplace is a small town in Texas.
We visited the president's birthplace.
The birthplace of the song is a village.

easy.def: A small, soft bread.
examples: I ate a biscuit.
The biscuit is warm.
She baked biscuits.

more.def: A small, soft, round bread that is baked quickly.
examples: I ate a warm biscuit with butter.
Grandma baked biscuits for breakfast.
He split the biscuit and added jam.

easy.def: A leader in some churches.
examples: The bishop gave a talk.
The bishop wore a tall hat.
The bishop visited.

more.def: A senior leader in some churches.
examples: The bishop visited our church on Sunday.
A bishop wears a tall hat.
The bishop gave a blessing.

easy.def: A piece in the game of chess.
examples: I moved my bishop.
The bishop is next to the king.
Bishops move on a slant.

more.def: A piece in chess that can move any distance on a slant.
examples: I moved my bishop across the board.
The bishop captured the knight.
A bishop stays on the same color of squares.

easy.def: A large, shaggy animal like a buffalo.
examples: A bison ate grass.
The bison is big.
We saw a bison.

more.def: A large, shaggy wild animal with a big head and a hump on its back, found on the grasslands of North America.
examples: A herd of bison grazed on the open prairie.
The bison has a big head and a hump on its shoulders.
Long ago, millions of bison roamed the plains.

easy.def: A small piece or amount.
examples: I ate a bit of cake.
Add a bit of salt.
A bit of paper.

more.def: A small piece or a small amount of something.
examples: I found a bit of string on the floor.
Add a bit more water to the soup.
She was a bit shy on her first day.

easy.def: To use your teeth to cut or hold.
examples: I bite the apple.
The dog bit the toy.
Do not bite your pencil.

more.def: To use your teeth to cut, hold or crush something.
examples: Bite the apple and chew it well.
The puppy bit the rope toy.
Mosquitoes bite at night.

easy.def: A mouthful of food.
examples: Take a bite.
One bite of cake.
I took a bite of the apple.

more.def: A small amount of food taken into the mouth at one time.
examples: She took a big bite of the sandwich.
Have a bite of my pie.
He saved one bite for later.

easy.def: A small hurt from a bug or animal.
examples: I have a mosquito bite.
The bite is small.
A bee bite itches.

more.def: A small cut or sting made by an insect or animal.
examples: The mosquito bite on my arm itched.
The dog's bite did not break the skin.
He put cream on the bite.

easy.def: Very small.
examples: I saw a bitsy bug.
I saw the bitsy puppy.
A bitsy bug crawled by.

more.def: Very small.
examples: A bitsy bug crawled on the leaf.
The bitsy puppy fit in my hand.
She wore bitsy earrings.

easy.def: Having a sharp, unpleasant taste.
examples: The medicine tastes bitter.
The coffee was bitter.
The seeds are bitter.

more.def: Having a strong, sharp taste that is not sweet.
examples: The medicine tasted bitter.
Lemon peel can taste bitter.
The coffee was too bitter for me.

easy.def: Very cold.
examples: The wind is bitter.
It was a bitter day.
We felt the bitter cold.

more.def: Extremely cold and sharp.
examples: A bitter wind blew across the lake.
It was a bitter winter night.
We wore thick coats against the bitter cold.

easy.def: A sharp taste that is not sweet.
examples: I did not like the bitterness of the lemon peel.
Dark chocolate has a little bitterness.
The coffee had a bitterness.

more.def: A sharp taste that is not sweet, or a lasting feeling of anger about something unfair.
examples: The bitterness of the strong tea made me frown.
She spoke of the old fight with bitterness.
Bitterness in his heart faded when they made up.

easy.def: Both sweet and sad at the same time.
examples: It was a bittersweet day.
A bittersweet goodbye.
The bittersweet ending.

more.def: Mixing happiness with sadness.
examples: The last day of school was bittersweet.
She felt bittersweet as she left her old home.
The chocolate had a bittersweet taste.

easy.def: Very strange.
examples: The dream was bizarre.
A bizarre noise came.
He wore a bizarre hat.

more.def: Very odd and unusual.
examples: I had a bizarre dream about a flying cat.
A bizarre noise came from the attic.
He wore a bizarre hat with feathers.
